### NFC Championship Game: at (2) Green Bay Packers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: NFC Championship Game: at (2) Green Bay Packers")]

After their big win over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys"), the Giants traveled to [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field") to face the second-seeded [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") on a freezing night. With a gametime temperature of -1 degree and a -23 degree windchill, it was the third-coldest NFL game in terms of windchill, behind the 1967 [Ice Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_NFL_Championship_Game "1967 NFL Championship Game") between the Cowboys and the Packers and the January 1982 [Freezer Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freezer_Bowl "Freezer Bowl") between the Chargers and the Bengals (which holds the record with a -59 degree windchill). While the Giants were steadily gaining more respect throughout the league after their upset of the Cowboys, most analysts and pundits predicted the Packers to win and represent the NFC in the Super Bowl.

The Packers won the toss and received the opening kickoff, but after two [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completions, the Packers failed to move the ball further and punted. The Giants offense opened the game with running back [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") plowing into cornerback [Charles Woodson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Woodson "Charles Woodson") on a five-yard run. With the help of three receptions by receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress"), the Giants entered the red zone when they survived a potential turnover. While being held by a lineman on a third-down play, [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") threw the ball straight to lineman [Cullen Jenkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullen_Jenkins "Cullen Jenkins"), but he dropped the potential interception, and instead the Giants got on the board first with kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") getting a 29-yard field goal. The Giants kept the ball for most of the 1st quarter, leading 3–0 at the end of the quarter.

In the 2nd quarter, the Packers defense shut the Giants' passing game down after two more completions to [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress"), so the Giants settled for another Tynes field goal at 11:41 left in the half. The Giants led 6–0, and appeared to be in good position for their next drive when [Koren Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koren_Robinson "Koren Robinson") muffed the ensuing kickoff and fell on it at the Packers's 10-yard line. However, on the first play of the Packers' next drive, [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") pump-faked, then threw a 90-yard TD pass to [Donald Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Driver "Donald Driver"), who had beaten blown coverage by cornerback [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster") before outrunning safety [Gibril Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibril_Wilson "Gibril Wilson") down the right sideline, and the Packers led 7–6. The teams then exchanged punts before the Packers received great field position at the Giants's 47-yard line. The Packers advanced into the red zone and faced a 3rd and 8 from the Giants 19-yard line. Favre found backup running back [Brandon Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jackson_(American_football) "Brandon Jackson (American football)") in the flat with lineman [Jason Spitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Spitz "Jason Spitz") out in front to block, but somehow, middle linebacker [Antonio Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Pierce "Antonio Pierce") grabbed hold of Jackson to prevent him from advancing before [Dave Tollefson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Tollefson "Dave Tollefson") could help him make the tackle. Green Bay settled for kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") making a 36-yard field goal to give the Packers a 10–6 lead with 1:34 left in the half. On the Giants's next drive, Manning found Burress deep for a 32-yard pass on his 7th reception of the day, but an [A. J. Hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._J._Hawk "A. J. Hawk") sack on fourth down prevented the Giants from scoring. The Packers led 10–6 at the half.

The Giants got the ball first in the 3rd quarter, and had a successful drive that ended with a [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") 1-yard TD run. The Giants led 13–10. This drive nearly ended with an interception with [Al Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Harris_(cornerback) "Al Harris (cornerback)") intercepting another Eli Manning pass intended for Burress, but he committed pass interference to make the interception, so the play was nullified. In the next Packers drive, after a [Sam Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Madison "Sam Madison") penalty, [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") threw a 12-yard TD pass to tight end [Donald Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Lee_(American_football) "Donald Lee (American football)"). The Packers led 17–13. The Giants responded in their next drive by driving to the four-yard line after a 23-yard reception by [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer") (which was challenged by Green Bay and upheld). From the Packers's 4-yard line, Manning then handed off to [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw"), who went off tackle right but got caught in a stalemate at the one-yard line. In a heads-up play, right tackle [Kareem McKenzie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareem_McKenzie "Kareem McKenzie") grabbed Bradshaw and dragged him into the end zone with him, resulting in a touchdown. The Giants led 20–17 with 2:12 left in the 3rd quarter.

For the remainder of regulation, the game would be defined by potentially crushing mistakes by the Giants that prevented them from entirely capitalizing on the Packers's failures to penetrate the Giants defense. On the next drive, Brett Favre avoided the Giants pass rush and threw an interception to [R. W. McQuarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._W._McQuarters "R. W. McQuarters"), but McQuarters never went down and was fumbled upon being tackled, with the loose ball bouncing straight to offensive lineman [Mark Tauscher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Tauscher "Mark Tauscher") at the 19-yard line. The Giants defense held, and with 11:46 left in the game, Packers kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") hit a 37-yard field goal to tie the game at 20–20. On the Giants' next drive, after not converting for a 1st down, the Giants were at 4th and 5. The Giants failed to convert, however a Packers penalty gave the Giants a 1st down. the Giants advanced to the Packers's 28-yard line when Eli Manning went for the touchdown to Plaxico Burress, when Al Harris finally made a play and broke up the pass. The Giants then went for a field goal, but with 6:49 left in the game, [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") missed a 43-yard field goal attempt. The Packers's next two drives went three-and-out before they punted to the Giants with 2:30 left. Packers punter [Jon Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Ryan "Jon Ryan")'s next punt went only 31 yards to the Packers's 48-yard line, but R. W. McQuarters fumbled the punt return, with [Domenik Hixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domenik_Hixon "Domenik Hixon") saving a turnover by recovering the ball at the 48-yard line. On the next play, Ahmad Bradshaw broke through the Packers's defense for what appeared to be a 48-yard touchdown run, but the play was nullified due to a holding penalty. Undaunted, Manning found [Steve Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Smith_(wide_receiver,_born_1985) "Steve Smith (wide receiver, born 1985)") for completions of 14 and 11 yards before the Giants killed time for Lawrence Tynes to attempt a game-winning 36-yard field goal. On the last play of regulation, however, Giants long snapper [Jay Alford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Alford "Jay Alford") had a low snap, and Tynes shanked the kick wide left on an attempt that was not even close to the uprights. The Giants and Packers went into overtime with the game tied at 20–20. The Packers won the coin toss and got the ball first.

For much of the game, cornerback [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster") had been playing with a massive chip on his shoulder. While the Giants coaches had tried to encourage him and assure him that he would get another opportunity, he remained angry over his poor play resulting in Brett Favre's 90-yard touchdown to Donald Driver and wanted to make a big play to make up for it. He finally got an opportunity on the second play of overtime. The Packers called an out pattern play for Driver, where Donald Lee would shift to fullback and attempt to deceive the Giants defense into believing that he would be a lead blocker on a running play (they had previously called this play twice before in the game, with the play being successful both times). Favre dropped back, and in a bonehead play that helped to define his legacy as a "gunslinger," threw the ball straight towards Webster, who was in position against Driver. Webster took advantage of his long-awaited opportunity and intercepted the pass, and went five yards before Driver dragged him down, which gave the Giants the ball in Packer territory. The Giants failed to convert on 3rd down and decided to go for the field goal. Although he had missed his previous two attempts, Tynes, like Webster before him, also wanted another opportunity and sprinted straight onto the field for a 47-yard attempt with 12:29 left in OT. Before Tynes's attempt, no kicker had made a field goal of over 40 yards with the game time temperature below freezing. Tynes's attempt initially went wide of the right goalpost, but the wind hooked it left and the kick went just over the crossbar for the game-winning field goal, and the Giants became the 2007 NFC Champions.

The Giants beat the Packers, 23–20. The Giants victory was the first championship win over the Packers since 1938. The Packers have a 4–2 record over the Giants in NFL/NFC Championship series. The win also marked the Giants' 10th straight road win and their 4th straight NFC Championship victory.

For the Giants, [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") went 21–40 for 251 yards. Although he didn't throw a touchdown, he avoided an interception for the third straight playoff game. It was generally agreed by critics after the game that he outplayed Favre, making another instance where he outplayed a quarterback considered far superior to him in the lead-up to the contest. [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") added 67 yards on 21 carries with a touchdown, while [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw") ran 16 times for 63 yards and a touchdown. [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") caught 11 passes for 151 yards. Along with his 200+ yard receiving performance in 2002 against the Falcons while a member of the Steelers, it is considered by many to be his single greatest game as a receiver.

While the Giants defense didn't have a sack in this contest, they held the Packers to just 28 yards rushing. Former Giants running back [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_(running_back) "Ryan Grant (running back)"), who had run for 201 yards against the Seahawks the previous week, ran for just 29 yards against his former team.

The game was [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre")'s final game as a Green Bay Packer, with whom he played with for 16 seasons. He appeared to retire for good during the offseason, but instead announced just before the season started that he wanted to play again. Because the Packers spent the offseason after the retirement announcement preparing [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") for the starting job, Favre became expendable and was traded to the Jets.

During the game, Giants coach [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin") caught frostbite. His increasingly red face due to the freezing conditions and frostbite received considerable attention from TV cameras during the game.

The New York Giants were headed to [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII") to face the 2007 AFC Champions [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") who were [undefeated at 18–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots_season "2007 New England Patriots season"). on February 3, 2008.

### Super Bowl XLII: vs. (A1) New England Patriots

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Super Bowl XLII: vs. (A1) New England Patriots")]

Two weeks after their [NFC Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Championship "NFC Championship") victory over the Packers, the Giants flew to the [University of Phoenix Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Phoenix_Stadium "University of Phoenix Stadium") for [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII") against the undefeated AFC Champions, the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots"), in a rematch of [Week 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots-New_York_Giants_game "2007 New England Patriots-New York Giants game"). That game had ended with the Patriots winning a very close game after coming back, and would prove to be a sign of things to come, but with a reverse ending.

After calling tails to win the coin toss, the Giants started the game with the longest opening drive in Super Bowl history, a 16-play, 77-yard march that consumed 9 minutes, 59 seconds and featured four third-down conversions, the most ever on a Super Bowl opening drive. But New England halted the drive at their own 14-yard line, where New York delivered the first punch with kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") nailing a 32-yard field goal for the only score of the period.

In the second quarter, the Patriots responded with RB [Laurence Maroney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Maroney "Laurence Maroney") getting a 1-yard TD run for the only score of the period. After a scoreless third quarter, the Giants regained the lead with QB [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completing a 5-yard TD pass to WR [David Tyree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tyree "David Tyree"). New England retook the lead with QB [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") completing a 6-yard TD pass to WR [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss"). Afterwards, with only 2 minutes and 40 seconds left, Manning led his Giants from their own 17-yard line all the way to the Patriots' 13-yard line, featuring a 4th down conversion (a one-yard run by Brandon Jacobs on 4th and inches) and even [Eli escaping a sure-fire sack & completing a 32-yard pass to Tyree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmet_Catch "Helmet Catch"), where he would hook up with WR [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") for the game-winning TD pass. The defense after that didn't even allow a single yard, as Brady was sacked once and threw 3 incomplete passes, turning the ball over on downs.

[![Image 12: Group of men and women, dressed in formal suits, standing on the White House's stairs](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Bush_%26_Cheney_with_NY_Giants_20080430-6_giants1-515h.jpg/250px-Bush_%26_Cheney_with_NY_Giants_20080430-6_giants1-515h.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bush_%26_Cheney_with_NY_Giants_20080430-6_giants1-515h.jpg)

The Giants visiting the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in honor of their Super Bowl victory on April 30, 2008.

With the win, the Giants finished their championship season with an overall record of 14–6. They became the third team (after the 1993 Cowboys and 2001 Patriots) to win the Super Bowl after beginning the season 0–2 and were the first NFC Wild Card to win the Super Bowl. The victory also gave them their 11th-straight road win (an NFL record).

Eli Manning was named the game's MVP after completing 19 of 34 passes for 255 yards, 2 touchdowns, and an interception; a majority of his offense came in the decisive fourth quarter, completing nine of 14 passes for 152 yards and both touchdowns. The defense had a stellar performance, sacking Patriots QB [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") five times.

Coach [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin") became the third oldest head coach to win the Super Bowl (61 years and 156 days). Punter [Jeff Feagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Feagles "Jeff Feagles") was the oldest player to play in a Super Bowl, let alone win one.

Eli and [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") became the first brother QBs to become back-to-back [Super Bowl winners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_winners "Super Bowl winners") and [Super Bowl MVPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_MVP "Super Bowl MVP").

*   The New York Giants lost to the Dallas Cowboys (twice), Green Bay Packers, and New England Patriots in the regular season but defeated them all in the post-season. In fact, the Minnesota Vikings are the only team that the Giants played during the 2007 season that the Giants did not defeat at least once (The Vikings did not make the playoffs and defeated the Giants in their only meeting during the regular season)
*   Of the New York Giants 10 victories the combined record of all teams were 60–100 (.375).
*   Of the New York Giants 10 victories 7 games were against teams below .500 that had a combined record of 35–77 (.313).
*   Of the New York Giants 10 victories 3 games were against teams above .500 that had a combined record of 25–23 (.521).
*   Of the New York Giants 6 losses the combined record of all teams were 51–29 (.638).
*   Of the New York Giants 4 post-season victories the combined record of all opponents (including playoffs) were 54–13 (.806).
*   The New York Giants combined regular season opponents records were 102–106 (.490).
*   The New York Giants total regular and post-season opponents (TB 9–7, playoffs only: GB 1–0 & NE 2–0) records were 114–113 (.502).
*   Peyton and Eli Manning are the first brothers to be named MVP of the Super Bowl, at the same position, and in back-to-back years.
*   The New York Giants trailed in all four post-season games, coming back to win all four. The Giants trailed in the fourth quarter in 2 out of the 4 games.
*   The Giants NFC Championship victory was their first win over the Packers in the playoffs since 1938. The Packers have a 4–2 record over the Giants in NFL/NFC Championship series.
*   The New York Giants played the New England Patriots at the end of the pre-season, regular season and post-season (Super Bowl XLII) during the 2007 season. This marks the third time that the Giants played a team that they would later face in the Super Bowl. Their record is 1–2 against these opponents in the regular season and 3–0 in the Super Bowl.
*   Ended the season with an 11-game road winning streak including playoffs. (the Week 8 game in London vs. the Dolphins and Super Bowl XLII in Arizona were both considered "away" games for the Giants. The Week 5 game vs. the Jets in Giants Stadium was considered a "home" game for the Giants.)
*   Prevented the Patriots from achieving what would have been the second undefeated season, and the first 19–0 season. (The first, and to date the only, was the [1972 Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Miami_Dolphins_season "1972 Miami Dolphins season"), although they finished 17–0)
*   Had only one starting Pro Bowler (Osi Umenyiora), fewest among Super Bowl champs.
*   All of their post-season games were announced by Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, due to each game being the perceived "marquee matchup" for Fox's coverage slate, along with the network holding broadcast rights for Super Bowl XLII.
*   The only time the Giants and the [Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers") met in the 2007 season was in the postseason.

Super Bowl XLII DVD
-------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Super Bowl XLII DVD")]

The official DVD of [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII") was released on February 26, 2008. The DVD covered the entire 2007 New York Giants season, as well as special features including the [NFL Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Network "NFL Network") postgame commentary, the halftime show in its entirety, the Media Day highlights, the [NFC Divisional Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#NFC_Divisional_Game:_at_Dallas_Cowboys) and [NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#NFC_Championship_Game:_at_Green_Bay_Packers) highlights, profiles on [Mathias Kiwanuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathias_Kiwanuka "Mathias Kiwanuka") and [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin"), and features on [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") and [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan").

"Stomp You Out" was the unofficial team motto of the 2007 New York Giants - especially their defense, which led the NFL with 52 sacks that season. It was started and perpetuated by Michael Strahan, saying he wanted to stomp out all of his opponents. During their playoff run, a relatively unknown motto was catapulted to national exposure as the Giants kept winning. The phrase remains a rallying cry for Giants fans to this day, much to the chagrin of their opponents, especially the Dallas Cowboys and the New England Patriots. At Strahan's 2014 Hall of Fame induction speech, he said, "Not only did we win the game [Super Bowl XLII], but we stomped them out!" much to the delight of Giants fans and players present.

9.title: Giants vs. Packers: Stats & Anecdotes
9.description: Giants.com's Michael Eisen gives you his notes, stats and anecdotes from the Giants 37-20 win over the Packers!
9.content:
Notes and statistics from the Giants' 37-20 NFC Divisional Playoff Game victory over the Green Bay Packers.

*The victory moved the Giants into the NFC Championship Game on Sunday in San Francisco against the 49ers, who defeated the Giants, 27-20, on Nov. 13 in Candlestick Park.

*The Giants won a playoff game in Lambeau Field for the second time in four seasons to become the first visiting team to win two postseason games here - and they did it in consecutive Packers postseason home games.

*This was the third time the Giants eliminated the defending Super Bowl champion from the playoffs. In 1985, the defeated the 49ers in an NFC Wild Card Game in Giants Stadium, 17-3, and five years later, they beat the Niners in San Francisco in the NFC Championship Game, 15-13.

*No defending Super Bowl champion has won a playoff game since 2005, when New England defeated Jacksonville in a wild card game before losing a divisional playoff game in Denver.

*The Giants enjoyed payback for the 38-35 loss the Packers pinned on them on Dec. 4. This was the second time the Giants lost to a team that finished 15-1 or better in the regular season, but won a postseason rematch. In 2007, they lost the regular season finale to 16-0 New England, 38-35, but reversed the outcome with a 17-14 victory in Super Bowl XLII.

*The Giants became the first No. 4 seed in the NFC to defeat a No. 1 seed in the divisional round of the playoffs. The NFC fourth seeds are now 1-8 in such games and 5-15 overall, including Denver's loss at New England Saturday night. NFC No. 1 seeds were 19-0 in the divisional round from 1988-2006. In the last five seasons, they are 1-4.

*The Giants' all-time postseason record is 22-24.

*The Giants are 5-6 in the divisional round of the playoffs since the 1970 merger, including 2-4 as visitors. They won their last two road games, including a 21-17 defeat the Cowboys in Dallas on Jan. 13, 2008, on their way to Super Bowl XLII.

*This was the seventh postseason meeting between the Giants and Packers. The first five meetings were in NFL Championship Games, plus the 2007 title game. The Packers lead the postseason series, 4-3.

*The Giants are 5-4 in Lambeau Field, 3-3 in the regular season and 2-1 in the postseason.

*This was the fifth time the Giants and Packers met in the regular season and in the playoffs in the same season. It also happened in 1938, 1944, 1961 and 2007. The Giants won three of the five postseason games.

*The 37 points was the Giants' fifth-highest total in a postseason game and the most points they scored since a 39-38 wild card loss in San Francisco on Jan. 5, 2003. It was their highest total in a playoff victory since the 41-0 rout of Minnesota in the 2000 NFC Championship Game.

*The Giants scored 17 points in the fourth quarter, their highest-scoring final quarter in a postseason game since Dec. 9, 1934, when they put 24 points on the board in a 30-13 victory over the Chicago Bears in the NFL Championship Game – better known as the "Sneakers Game."

*The teams combined to score 57 points, the fourth highest-scoring postseason game in Giants history. The record is 77 points (49ers 39, Giants 38) at San Francisco on Jan. 5, 2003.

*The Giants' 420 net yards was their fourth-highest total in a postseason game. They gained 442 yards last week vs. Atlanta.

*The Giants' 325 net passing yards was their third-highest total in a postseason game and the most they had in the playoffs since throwing for 327 yards at San Francisco on Jan. 5, 2003.

*The Giants' defense held the Packers to 20 points – 20 below their regular season average in Lambeau. Green Bay led the NFL with 560 points, or 35.0 a game.

*The Packers failed on a fourth-down conversion attempt in the fourth quarter when Aaron Rodgers was sacked for a six-yard loss by Michael Boley. The Giants have stopped five consecutive opponent fourth-down conversion attempts, including one against Dallas in the regular season finale and three last week vs. Atlanta.

*This was the Giants' sixth postseason victory under head coach Tom Coughlin. He is second in Giants history in playoff victories, trailing only Bill Parcells, who had eight.

*Coughlin is 10-7 overall in the postseason. The 10 victories tie him with Philadelphia's Andy Reid for second among active coaches. New England's Bill Belichick is first with 16.

*Coughlin has 152 combined regular season and postseason victories. That places him 19th in NFL history, one behind Giants Hall of Fame Coach Steve Owen.

*The Giants are 4-1 in road playoff games under Coughlin. Overall, Coughlin is 6-4 on the road in postseason games with the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Giants. The sixth victory broke a tie with Hall of Famer and former Washington Coach Joe Gibbs and moved Coughlin into second place on the NFL's career list. Another member of the Hall of Fame, former Dallas Coach Tom Landry, was 7-7 in road playoff games.

*Coughlin is 0-3 against Green Bay's Mike McCarthy in the regular season and 2-0 in the playoffs.

*Eli Manning completed 21 of 33 passes for 330 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Manning's 21 completions tied for his second-highest total in a postseason game (he also had 21 against the Packers in Lambeau in the 2007 NFC Championship Game and a career-high 23 last week in the wild card victory over Atlanta).

*Manning now has 157 postseason completions, which ties Phil Simms for first place on the Giants' career postseason list.

*Manning's 330 yards were a career postseason high and the third-highest total by a Giants quarterback in a playoff game. Kerry Collins threw for 381 yards in the 2000 NFC Championship Game and for 342 yards in a wild card game in San Francisco on Jan. 5, 2003.

*Manning's previous postseason high was 277 yards last week against Atlanta.

*Manning increased his career postseason yardage total to 1,904, which moves him past Simms (1,679) and into first place on the Giants' all-time list.

*Manning's three touchdown passes tied his career postseason high set last week and increased his total to 14, extending his own franchise postseason record.

*Manning joined Simms, Collins and Scott Brunner as the only Giants quarterback to throw at least three touchdown passes in at least two postseason games.

*Manning's 66-yard touchdown pass to Hakeem Nicks in the first quarter was the fourth-longest postseason play in Giants history and the second in as many weeks that was at least that long.

Manning and Nicks tied the record last week with a completion against Atlanta of 72 yards, the mark first set by a Brunner-to-Earnest Gray pass on Jan. 3, 1982 at San Francisco. In third place is a 67-yard pass by Charlie Conerly to Frank Gifford against the Chicago Bears on Dec 30, 1956.

*Nicks caught seven passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns. The 165 yards were the second-highest total by a Giant in a postseason game. Bob Schnelker holds the record with 175 receiving yards at Baltimore on Dec. 27, 1959.

*Nicks has 280 receiving postseason receiving yards, which puts him in fifth place on the Giants' career list – after just two games.

*Nicks' average of 23.57 yards per catch was the highest ever by a Giant with more than four receptions in a postseason game.

*Nicks caught two touchdown passes in the Giants' victory over Atlanta last week. He joins Amani Toomer as the only Giant to score at least two touchdowns in at least two postseason games.

*Nicks' four postseason receiving touchdowns are second in Giants history behind Toomer's seven.

*Nicks became Manning's most frequent postseason touchdown target with four. Toomer and Plaxico Burress each caught three Manning playoff touchdown passes.

*Victor Cruz had five receptions for 74 yards, while Mario Manningham had three for 31 yards, including his second touchdown in as many weeks.

*Lawrence Tynes scored 13 points (three field goals and four extra points) to increase his Giants career postseason total to 44. That moved him past Brad Daluiso and Ken Strong (36 each) and Amani Toomer (42) and into first place on the franchise's career postseason scoring list.

*Tynes' four field goal attempts (he had one blocked) gave him 13 in the postseason, a Giants record. His nine postseason field goals tie Brad Daluiso for first place.

*Tynes now owns the Giants' record for career postseason extra points attempted and made (17 each).

*Brandon Jacobs scored the Giants' final touchdown on a 14-yard run with 2:36 remaining. It was his fifth postseason touchdown (fourth rushing), which broke a tie with Joe Morris and Strong and moved him into second place on the Giants' career postseason list. Toomer is first with seven playoff touchdowns.

*Jacobs' four rushing touchdowns put him in a first-place tie with Morris.

*Defensive end Osi Umenyiora and linebacker Boley each had two sacks. They became the seventh and eighth Giants with at least two sacks in a postseason game. Boley's sacks were the first of his postseason career. He had one sack in the regular season. Umenyiora has five sacks in the three games since he returned from an ankle injury.

*McCarthy won a replay challenge with 8:24 remaining in the first quarter. On the kickoff following Tynes' first field goal, rookie returner Randall Cobb fumbled the ball, which was recovered by the Giants. McCarthy challenged, saying Cobb was down by contact prior to losing the ball. After review, referee Bill Leavy reversed the call on the field and the Packers retained possession.

*Coughlin lost a replay challenge with 1:34 remaining in the first quarter, when Rodgers completed a pass to Greg Jennings, who fumbled. The ball was recovered by the Giants, but the officials ruled Jennings was down by contact before losing the ball. Coughlin challenged the ruling, but after review, Leavy upheld the ball on the field, despite replays that seemed to show Jennings lost the ball before he was down. Coughlin has lost his last eight replay challenges, including two in the regular season game against Green Bay.

*Brad Jones blocked Tynes' 40-yard field goal attempt in the second quarter. It was the third time this season a Tynes field goal attempt was blocked. The Redskins' Brian Orakpo blocked a 38-yard attempt by Tynes on Sept. 11 in Washington and Buffalo's Alex Carrington got a hand on his 50-yard attempt in MetLife Stadium on Oct. 16.

*The Giants' inactive players were linebacker Mark Herzlich, wide receiver Ramses Barden, running back Da'Rel Scott, offensive linemen Jim Cordle and James Brewer, and defensive linemen Jimmy Kennedy and Justin Trattou.

The **2007 Green Bay Packers season** was the franchise's 89th overall and 87th season in the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). The Packers finished the regular season with a 13–3 record and clinched their first winning season, playoff appearance and division title since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2004 Green Bay Packers season"). They received for the first time since [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1997 Green Bay Packers season") a [bye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye_(sports) "Bye (sports)") for the first round of the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_playoffs,_2007%E2%80%9308 "NFL playoffs, 2007–08"), and won their divisional round playoff game to advance to the franchise's first [NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Championship_Game "NFC Championship Game") in 10 years. The Packers ultimately lost the NFC Championship game to the eventual [Super Bowl champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII")[New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"). It was the first time the Packers had lost a home NFC Championship game, and only their third home playoff loss ever. This was the last season for quarterback [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") as a Green Bay Packer, as he initially retired following the season but came out of retirement and was subsequently traded to the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_New_York_Jets_season "2008 New York Jets season") during the offseason.

This season also marked the 50th anniversary of the opening of the Packers' home stadium of [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field"). The Packers' tenure at Lambeau, now at 64 seasons, is the longest in NFL history at a single stadium, breaking the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears")' previous record of 50 seasons at [Wrigley Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrigley_Field "Wrigley Field") (1921–1970).

On February 2, 2007, [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") announced that he would return for the 2007 season. "I am so excited about coming back," the 37-year-old quarterback said on the website of _[The Sun Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sun\_Herald "The Sun Herald")_ in [Biloxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biloxi "Biloxi"), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"). He also commented, "We have a good nucleus of young players. We were 8–8 last year, and that's encouraging."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-returnNFL.com-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-returnPackers.com-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-returnSunHerald-3)

Ted Thompson, Green Bay's general manager, confirmed the news, saying, "The Packers are excited by his decision and look forward to a successful 2007 campaign."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-tedthompson-4) This would be, however, Brett Favre's last season with the Packers, after 16 years on the team.

The [2007 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFL_draft "2007 NFL draft") occurred on April 28–29. The Packers picked 16th overall, selecting [defensive tackle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_tackle "Defensive tackle")[Justin Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Harrell "Justin Harrell") in the first round.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-draftorder-5)

Reportedly, the Packers were in talks with [Oakland Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders "Oakland Raiders") wide receiver [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss") at the behest of Brett Favre.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-mosstrade-6) If the Packers had made the move to acquire the 30-year-old [wide receiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_receiver "Wide receiver"), the trade would no doubt have been a controversial one, as Moss had a long and storied history with the Green Bay franchise.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-mosstrade-6) While Moss's salary was high, Green Bay, at the time, reportedly had $24 million of cap space, and could have absorbed his contract easily.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-mosstrade2-7) These rumors were put to an end on April 29, 2007, when Oakland dealt Moss to New England for a 4th round draft pick.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-mossNE-8) In the days following the NFL draft, Favre was upset concerning Green Bay's inability to acquire Moss.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-upsetFavre-9) Favre was reportedly so upset that his agent requested that the Packers trade him.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-upsetFavre-9) Coach Mike McCarthy was able to calm Favre down over the phone, and Favre eventually admitted that while he wanted to win, he did not want to be traded in order to do so.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-upsetFavre-9)

### Week 1: vs. Philadelphia Eagles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Week 1: vs. Philadelphia Eagles")]

The Packers began their season at home against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"). In the first quarter, Green Bay's [Jarrett Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarrett_Bush "Jarrett Bush") recovered the Eagles' [Greg Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Lewis_(wide_receiver) "Greg Lewis (wide receiver)")'s muffed punt in the end zone for a touchdown. The contest was tied in the closing minutes but the Eagles again muffed a punt return, setting up a 42-yard kick from Packers rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby"). This was the only game the Packers did not score an offensive touchdown. Crosby was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-SpecialTeamsPlayeroftheWeek-13) Crosby is the only player in league history to boot a 50-plus-yard field goal and game winning field goal in the final minute in his first NFL game.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-Onlykicker-14)

### Week 2: at New York Giants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Week 2: at New York Giants")]

[![Image 14: An aerial view of American football players lined up on a green field marked with white lines and numbers](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/GBNYShotgun.jpg/250px-GBNYShotgun.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GBNYShotgun.jpg)

The Packers in the [shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun_formation "Shotgun formation")

Playing a close game until the fourth quarter, the Packers took a commanding lead late in the game (racking up 21 points in the final fifteen minutes) and winning the game 35–13. Early in the 4th quarter, Favre capped off a drive with a pass to the outside of the endzone to Donald Lee, and then followed it up with a 10-yard pass to Donald Driver by the goalpost for a score after the Giants fumbled the ensuing kickoff deep in their own territory. In the victory, Brett Favre threw for 286 yards and 3 touchdowns and gave him his 149th career win as a starter, the most by any [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") in NFL history, surpassing [John Elway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway"). Favre was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week for games played September 16–17.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-PlayeroftheWeek-15) Mike McCarthy was voted the Motorola NFL Coach of the Week.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-CoachoftheWeek-16)

### Week 3: vs. San Diego Chargers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Week 3: vs. San Diego Chargers")]

Quarterback Brett Favre threw three touchdown passes against the [Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Chargers "San Diego Chargers") in the victory, bringing his career total to 420 and tying [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s career touchdown record. With just over two minutes remaining in the game and San Diego leading 21–17, Favre found wide receiver [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") for a 57-yard catch and run across the middle of the field for the go-ahead score. On the Chargers ensuing drive, linebacker Nick Barnett intercepted a [Philip Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Rivers "Philip Rivers") pass and returned it to the San Diego 1-yard line setting up the Packers final score and a 10-point lead. Barnett was voted the GMC Defensive Player of the Week for games played on September 23 – 24.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-DefensivePlayeroftheWeek-17) This win made the Packers the only team to have missed the playoffs the previous season to return to open 3–0 against teams that made the playoffs the year before.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-first3and0-18)

### Week 4: at Minnesota Vikings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Week 4: at Minnesota Vikings")]

[![Image 15: A large digital screen displays Brett Favre's record-breaking passing touchdown count in a stadium filled with spectators](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/09.30.07_favre_421TD.JPG/250px-09.30.07_favre_421TD.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:09.30.07_favre_421TD.JPG)

[Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") broke [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s TD pass record during Week 4 at the HHH Metrodome

Coming off their home win over the Chargers, the Packers flew to the [Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_H._Humphrey_Metrodome "Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome") for an NFC North division game against [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings"). In the first quarter, QB [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") threw a 16-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") surpassing [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino") as the league's all-time leader in touchdown passes. He also became the league leader in pass attempts (8,393 at game's end).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-PassAttemptLeader-19) Favre was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week for the second time this season, having thrown for 344 yards and two touchdowns.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-PlayerOfTheWeek2-20)

With the win, the Packers stayed undefeated and improved to their first 4–0 start since 1998.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-undefeatedsince98-21)

### Week 5: vs. Chicago Bears

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Week 5: vs. Chicago Bears")]

Coming off a record-setting divisional road game against the Vikings, the Packers went home for a Sunday night divisional clash with their nemesis, the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"). This would be the 174th meeting between the two teams.

In the first quarter, Green Bay got off to a fast start by capping off the game's opening drive with rookie RB [DeShawn Wynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeShawn_Wynn "DeShawn Wynn") getting a 2-yard TD run for the only score of the period. In the second quarter, the Bears tied the game with RB [Cedric Benson's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_Benson "Cedric Benson") 10-yard TD run. The Packers would end the first half with QB [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completing a 41-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"), along with rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converting a 37-yard field goal.

In the third quarter, Chicago crept closer with kicker [Robbie Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Gould "Robbie Gould") converting a 44-yard field goal. Green Bay responded with Crosby kicking a 37-yard field goal, yet the Bears pulled to within three as QB [Brian Griese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Griese "Brian Griese") completed a 19-yard TD pass to TE [Greg Olsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Olsen_(American_football) "Greg Olsen (American football)"). In the fourth quarter, Chicago erased their deficit completely with Gould's 36-yard field goal and Griese's 34-yard TD pass to TE [Desmond Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmond_Clark "Desmond Clark").

With a turnover-plagued loss (5 turnovers on the night), the Packers fell to 4–1. Also, with two interceptions, Favre tied QB [George Blanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Blanda "George Blanda") at 277 for the most career interceptions.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-22) Also of note, [Brady Poppinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brady_Poppinga "Brady Poppinga") intercepted a pass in the fourth quarter, extending the streak of at least one Packer interception per game for the 11th consecutive game. This matched the longest streak in team history, which occurred during an 11-game stretch in 1984–1985.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-calhoun2-23)

### Week 6: vs. Washington Redskins

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Week 6: vs. Washington Redskins")]

On October 14, 2007 [Charles Woodson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Woodson "Charles Woodson") picked up a [Santana Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santana_Moss "Santana Moss") fumble and returned it 57 yards for a go-ahead touchdown in a 17–14 victory over the [Washington Redskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-24) He also recorded an interception in the game, his first of the season. This was the 12 straight game that Green Bay has recorded an interception, making it a new team record surpassing an 11-game stretch in 1984–1985.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-calhoun2-23)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-25) In the third quarter, Redskins safety [Sean Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Taylor "Sean Taylor") intercepted a Brett Favre pass making Favre the career interception leader in NFL history, eclipsing George Blanda's record of 277 interceptions. Favre threw two interceptions for the game.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-26) Woodson was named the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week for his performance versus the Redskins. It was the first time he has received this award.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-27)

With the win, the Packers entered its bye week at 5–1.

### Week 8: at Denver Broncos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Week 8: at Denver Broncos")]

Following their bye week, the Packers flew to Denver to take on the Broncos on [Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday_Night_Football "Monday Night Football"). In the first quarter, Bronco quarterback [Jay Cutler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler "Jay Cutler") opened the scoring with a 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Tony Scheffler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Scheffler "Tony Scheffler"). On the first play of the ensuing series [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completed a 79-yard touchdown to rookie wide receiver [James Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jones_(wide_receiver) "James Jones (wide receiver)"). In the second quarter, rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converted a 19-yard field goal, followed by a 26-yard field goal, and the Packers took a 13–7 lead into halftime.

In the third quarter, Broncos kicker [Jason Elam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Elam "Jason Elam") converted a 45-yard field goal to cut Green Bay's lead to 3 points. In the fourth quarter, after getting the ball back with 2:27 remaining in the game, Cutler led a drive that began on the Bronco seven-yard line down the length of the field to the Green Bay four-yard line. On a 3rd and 1 Cutler attempted a quarterback draw to win the game, but [Ryan Pickett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Pickett "Ryan Pickett") stopped Cutler for no gain on the play. With no time outs remaining Elam and the kicking unit ran onto the field and converted a field goal to tie the game on the final play of the quarter.

[Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") called heads and won the overtime coin toss, allowing Green Bay to receive the ball to begin overtime. On the first play, Favre threw an 82-yard touchdown pass to Jennings, who had outrun Bronco cornerback [Dré Bly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr%C3%A9_Bly "Dré Bly") for the catch. This was Favre's 13th TD pass of 75 yards or more, most of any player in NFL history.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-packers.com-28) Favre also becomes the first Packers player to throw two touchdown passes of 75 yards or more in the same game. Only three quarterbacks have accomplished the feat since 1990.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-packers.com-28)[Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_(running_back) "Ryan Grant (running back)") ran for 104 yards, the first Packer to break the 100 yard rushing mark this season.

With the win (their first ever in Denver), the Packers improved to 6–1. On November 1, 2007 [Aaron Kampman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Kampman "Aaron Kampman") was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Month for October, having recorded 5.5 sacks during that time period.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-29) Brett Favre was voted the Fedex Air and Ground NFL Player of the Week award for games played on October 28 – 29, the third time this season he has received this award.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-30) Wide receiver James Jones of the Packers was announced as the Diet Pepsi 2007 Rookie of the Week for games played on October 28–29. Jones made three receptions for 107 yards including a first-quarter 79-yard touchdown.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-31)

### Week 9: at Kansas City Chiefs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Week 9: at Kansas City Chiefs")]

Coming off their Monday Night road win over the Broncos, the Packers flew to [Arrowhead Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowhead_Stadium "Arrowhead Stadium") for a Week 9 interconference duel with the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"). After a scoreless first quarter, Green Bay drew first blood with rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") getting a 48-yard and a 36-yard field goal. However, the Chiefs would take the lead into halftime as RB [Larry Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Johnson_(running_back) "Larry Johnson (running back)") completed a 1-yard TD run.

In the third quarter, the Packers regained the lead as Favre completed a 13-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") for the only score of the period. In the fourth quarter, Kansas City regained the lead with QB [Damon Huard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damon_Huard "Damon Huard") completing a 30-yard TD pass to Johnson. Green Bay replied with Crosby kicking a 32-yard field goal, yet the Chiefs answered with Huard completing a 17-yard TD pass to TE [Tony Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Gonzalez "Tony Gonzalez") (with RB [Priest Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priest_Holmes "Priest Holmes") getting the 2-point conversion run). The Packers pulled back into the lead as Favre and Jennings hooked up again on a 60-yard TD pass. Afterwards, Crosby made a 45-yard field goal, and CB [Charles Woodson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Woodson "Charles Woodson") returned an interception 46 yards for a touchdown.

With the win, the Packers improved to 7–1. Brett Favre also became the third quarterback to defeat all of the other 31 NFL teams at least once. [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") and [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") had been the first two to do so, just hours apart, the week before.

The Packers scored 17 points in the final 3:05 on a defense that hadn't given up more than 20 all year.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-nfl.com-32) Favre joined [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") and [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") as quarterbacks who've beaten all 31 other teams in the NFL.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-nfl.com-32) Favre rallied the Packers to victory from a fourth-quarter deficit or tie for the fourth time this season and 40th in his career, second only to John Elway's 46 fourth-quarter comebacks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-33) The Packers have won 11 of their last 12 games, dating back to last season. Their sixth straight road wins tie for the second-longest away-from-home streak in team history.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-34)

### Week 10: vs. Minnesota Vikings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Week 10: vs. Minnesota Vikings")]

Playing their first home game since mid-October, the Packers hosted their division rivals, the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings").

In the first half, the first career touchdown[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-35) by [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_(running_back) "Ryan Grant (running back)") came on a 30-yard run and gave the Packers a 7–0 lead, and two field goals by Mason Crosby (a 39-yard field goal midway through the 2nd quarter and a 24-yard field goal at the end of the half) would provide all the first half scoring, as the Packers went to the locker room leading 13–0.

In the second half, Brett Favre threw a pair of third-quarter touchdown passes, one to Donald Lee and one to Ruvell Martin (which was Favre's 200th TD pass at Lambeau Field),[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sportinglife.com-36) giving the Packers a 27–0 lead. With an additional Martin touchdown catch in the 4th quarter, the Packers shut out the Vikings 34–0, their first shutout of 2007. The Packers defense held [Adrian Peterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Peterson "Adrian Peterson") to a season-low 45 yards on 11 carries a week after he set the NFL single-game rushing record with 296 yards against the San Diego Chargers.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-37) Grant became the first running back to reach the century mark against the Vikings this season, rushing for 119 yards on 25 carries, his career best.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sportinglife.com-36)

With the win, the Packers improved to 8–1, which matched the best start to a season in Brett Favre's career (in 1996 and 2002).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sportinglife.com-36) This game was the first time the Vikings had been shut out since 1991,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-38) and halted the Vikings’ NFL-record run of 260 consecutive regular-season games with a point.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-39) The game was Green Bay's first shutout of the Vikings in 94 games of the rivalry.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-40)

During the game, Favre became only the second NFL quarterback to throw for 60,000 yards in a career. He now has 60,257 yards' passing in his 17-year NFL career, second only to Dan Marino's career passing record of 61,361 yards.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-41) On November 15, 2007, the NFL announced Favre and running back Ryan Grant were voted the FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week for games played on November 11–12.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-42) Favre has received the FedEx Air award four times this season. Coach McCarthy was voted the Motorola NFL Coach of the Week for games played on November 11–12, the second time he has received the award this season.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-43)

### Week 11: vs. Carolina Panthers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Week 11: vs. Carolina Panthers")]

38-year-old Brett Favre faced off against 44-year-old Carolina quarterback [Vinny Testaverde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinny_Testaverde "Vinny Testaverde") in a game that featured the oldest starting quarterbacks duo in NFL history.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sports.yahoo.com-44) Favre threw 3 touchdown passes, and [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams") returned a punt 94-yard for another touchdown as Green Bay defeated the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") 31–17. It was Favre's 62nd career game with at least three touchdown passes, tying [Dan Marino's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino") record.

The win moved Green Bay to 9–1 on the season, its best start through the first 10 games since 1962.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sports.yahoo.com-44) This is also Favre's best 10 game start to a season in his career.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-45) Packers punt returner Tramon Williams was named Special Teams Players of the Week for games played the 11th week of the 2007 season (November 18–19).[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-46) Packers defensive tackle [Corey Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Williams_(American_football) "Corey Williams (American football)") was voted the GMC Defensive Player of the Week for games played on November 18–19. Williams posted four solo tackles, two sacks and two forced fumbles during the game.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-47)

### Week 12: at Detroit Lions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Week 12: at Detroit Lions")]

Coming off their home win over the Panthers, the Packers flew to [Ford Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Field "Ford Field") for a Week 12 Thanksgiving NFC North duel with the [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions"). Lions kicker [Jason Hanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Hanson "Jason Hanson") completed a 47-yard field goal, and followed it with a 41-yarder to give the Lions a 6–0 lead after the first quarter. [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") started the second quarter with an 11-yard TD pass to [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"). The Packers held on to the lead for the remainder of the game, winning 37–26. The win moved the Packers to 10–1 on the season.

Favre finished the game with 3 touchdowns, the 63rd time he has thrown 3 or more touchdowns in a game, breaking the record he held with [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino"). At one point during the game, Favre completed 20 consecutive passes, breaking the Packers team record of 18 (held by [Don Majkowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Majkowski "Don Majkowski") and [Lynn Dickey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Dickey "Lynn Dickey")).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-48) Favre threw for 381 passing yards, which was his seventh 300-yard passing game of the season, tying a career-high.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-49) For his performance, Favre was awarded Fox's Galloping Gobbler Award. Favre also was voted Fedex Air NFL Player of the Week, the fifth time this year he has received the award.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-50)

Green Bay has equaled its best 11-game record since 1929.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-51)

With the win, the Packers improved to 10–1 (the team's best start since 1962).
